#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script converted from Slurm
# Note: Flux does not support in-script directives for resource specification
# This script should be submitted with the following command:
# flux batch -N 1 -n 16 -t 8h --job-name=dsmc_job --output=logs/dsmc_job_{{id}}.out --error=logs/dsmc_job_{{id}}.err script.sh
#
# Resource specifications:
# -N 1         : 1 node (from -N 1)
# -n 16        : 16 cores/tasks (from -n 16)
# -t 8h        : 8 hour runtime (from -t 0-08:00)
# --job-name=dsmc_job : job name (derived from output file pattern)
# --output=logs/dsmc_job_{{id}}.out : stdout file with job ID
# --error=logs/dsmc_job_{{id}}.err : stderr file with job ID
#
# Note: Flux uses {{id}} for job ID instead of %j

# Original Slurm partition: shared
# Slurm: -p shared
# Note: Flux does not have partitions in the same way as Slurm
# Partition selection is handled through Flux's scheduling configuration
# Performance impact: Job scheduling priority depends on site-specific Flux configuration
# Consult site documentation for equivalent resource pools or queues

# Original Slurm memory per CPU: 512 MB
# Slurm: --mem-per-cpu 512
# Note: Flux memory specification can be done at submission:
# Add to submission command: --setattr=system.memory-per-task=512M
# Or total memory: --setattr=system.memory=8192M (512 MB × 16 cores)
# Performance impact: Without explicit memory specification, job may get default allocation
# which could be insufficient or excessive

# Original Slurm open-mode: append
# Slurm: --open-mode=append
# Note: Flux does not have a direct equivalent for --open-mode=append
# Performance impact: Output files will be truncated (overwritten) rather than appended
# If append behavior is critical, use shell redirection (>>) in the script
# or manage output files manually

# Load required modules
module load intel/19.0.5-fasrc01 openmpi/4.0.2-fasrc01 fftw/3.3.8-fasrc01 cmake/3.12.1-fasrc01 Anaconda3/2019.10 python/3.7.7-fasrc01
module list

# Environment variables for OpenMP threading
export OMP_PROC_BIND=spread
export OMP_PLACES=threads

# Set Julia thread count
# Note: SLURM_CPUS_ON_NODE is Slurm-specific
# Flux equivalent: Use FLUX_JOB_SIZE or set explicitly based on allocation
# For this job with 16 cores on 1 node:
export JULIA_NUM_THREADS=16
# Alternative: export JULIA_NUM_THREADS=${FLUX_JOB_SIZE}

echo "running...."

# Execute Julia script
julia RunCells.jl -l 0.001 -L 0.02

# Complete submission command:
# flux batch -N 1 -n 16 -t 8h \
#   --job-name=dsmc_job \
#   --output=logs/dsmc_job_{{id}}.out \
#   --error=logs/dsmc_job_{{id}}.err \
#   --setattr=system.memory=8192M \
#   script.sh

issues: The script correctly documents resource specifications and properly converts Slurm directives to Flux command-line options.

Memory specification is documented but not included in the primary submission command at the top. The complete submission command at the bottom includes '--setattr=system.memory=8192M' which is correct (16 cores × 512 MB = 8192 MB).

The JULIA_NUM_THREADS is hardcoded to 16. While correct for this specific job, using FLUX_JOB_SIZE environment variable would be more portable: 'export JULIA_NUM_THREADS=${FLUX_JOB_SIZE:-16}' with a fallback to 16.
The logs directory path is used but no check exists to ensure it exists before job submission. Consider adding 'mkdir -p logs' or validating the directory exists.
Output file pattern uses {{id}} which is correct for Flux, but should verify this syntax is supported in the specific Flux version being used.
The --open-mode=append behavior from Slurm is lost. If appending to existing logs is important for this workflow, the script should implement this with shell redirection or file management logic.
No cores-per-task specification. With -n 16 on -N 1, this allocates 16 tasks on 1 node. If the job actually needs 16 threads (as suggested by JULIA_NUM_THREADS=16), consider using -n 1 -c 16 instead.
The module loading may fail silently. Consider adding error checking after module loads.
The 8-hour runtime may be insufficient for some workloads. No checkpointing or restart capability is mentioned.

#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH -n 16 # Number of cores requested
#SBATCH -N 1 # Ensure that all cores are on one machine
#SBATCH -t 0-08:00 # Runtime in minutes
#SBATCH -p shared # Partition to submit to
#SBATCH --mem-per-cpu 512 # Memory per cpu in MB (see also ?mem-per-cpu)
#SBATCH --open-mode=append
#SBATCH -o logs/dsmc_job_%j.out # Standard out goes to this file
#SBATCH -e logs/dsmc_job_%j.err # Standard err goes to this filehostname

module load intel/19.0.5-fasrc01 openmpi/4.0.2-fasrc01 fftw/3.3.8-fasrc01 cmake/3.12.1-fasrc01 Anaconda3/2019.10 python/3.7.7-fasrc01
module list

export OMP_PROC_BIND=spread
export OMP_PLACES=threads
export JULIA_NUM_THREADS=$SLURM_CPUS_ON_NODE

echo "running...."

julia RunCells.jl -l 0.001 -L 0.02
